intro: An ancient {noun}, its surface worn smooth by centuries of unknown hands.
A weathered {noun}, half-buried when it was found, still faintly warm to the touch.
This {noun} hums faintly when held, as though something inside it is still awake.
No two accounts of this {noun} agree on where it came from, only that it was never meant to be found.
The {noun} is heavier than it looks, and colder than the air around it.
Strange markings cover the {noun}, in a script no scholar of this age can read.
Dust never seems to settle on this {noun}, no matter how long it sits untouched.
The {noun} was pried from something's grip. What, exactly, nobody wants to guess.
An old {noun}, bearing the marks of a craftsman long dead and a purpose long forgotten.
The {noun} once belonged to a traveler who vanished without a trace. It was the only thing left behind.
Whoever last owned this {noun} took great care of it. Whoever found it did not.
A faded name is carved into the {noun}, but the letters have been scratched through so violently that the reason is anyone's guess.
The {noun} shows signs of having been buried, broken, repaired, and buried again.
This {noun} was once found among the belongings of a man who had no memory of where he got it.
The {noun} bears a single dark stain that no amount of cleaning has managed to remove.
An old inscription on the {noun} reads like a warning, though the final words have been worn away.
The previous owner of this {noun} reportedly refused to let anyone else touch it.
The {noun} was recovered from the ruins of a place that no longer appears on any map.
Something about the {noun} suggests it was made for a hand much older than yours.
The {noun} has passed through many hands. Curiously, most of its owners met rather unfortunate ends.
Someone carved tally marks into the {noun}. There are far too many to guess what they were counting.
The {noun} still carries the faint scent of smoke, though no one can explain why.
An ancient {noun}, its surface worn smooth by generations of hands that are long gone.
The {noun} bears the crest of a noble dwarven clan that disappeared centuries ago.
The last known owner of this {noun} was a soldier who returned from war alone and never spoke of where he had been.
The {noun} was discovered in a locked chest. The chest had been buried beneath a church that does not exist anymore.
An old craftsman once called this {noun} his finest work. He destroyed every other piece he ever made.
The {noun} is covered in tiny scratches, as though someone spent years trying to write something into it.
Whoever carried this {noun} knew enough to keep it hidden. They were not careful enough to hide it forever.
The {noun} was passed down through a family for generations. The family is now extinct.
A faded ribbon is tied around the {noun}. It looks strangely well-preserved.
The {noun} was found in the possession of a thief who swore he had stolen it from himself.
The {noun} has been repaired more times than anyone can count, yet the oldest damage remains untouched.
Someone went to great lengths to erase the markings on the {noun}. A few still remain.
The {noun} was recovered from a battlefield long after the dead had been forgotten.
An inscription beneath the {noun} simply reads: 'Return this before it is too late.'
The {noun} belonged to an explorer who disappeared on the final day of his greatest expedition.
Whatever the {noun} was used for, its previous owner apparently considered it worth killing for.
The {noun} was found in a room with no doors and no other way out.
The previous owner of this {noun} left behind only a name, a grave, and several contradictory stories.
The {noun} has a small hollow inside it. Something was once hidden there.
An old prayer has been etched into the {noun}, but several of the words have been deliberately defaced.
The {noun} was found wrapped in a child's blanket, despite being far too old for either to have belonged together.
The {noun} feels strangely familiar, though you have never seen it before.
Someone once wore the {noun} close to their body. The marks it left behind suggest they did so for a very long time.
The {noun} survived a fire that destroyed everything around it. Its previous owner did not.
The {noun} was recovered from a grave that had been opened from the inside.
No one knows who made the {noun}. Several people, however, are certain they have seen it before.
The {noun} bears a maker's mark that belongs to a craftsman who supposedly never existed.
The previous owner of the {noun} was buried with it. Someone later decided they wanted it back.
The {noun} was once considered worthless. That opinion changed rather suddenly.
An old journal mentions this {noun} only once, followed by three pages that have been torn out.
The {noun} has changed hands countless times. Its oldest recorded owner died more than a century ago.
Someone scratched a single word into the {noun}: 'Again.'
curse: Those who carried it before you did not carry it for long.
It resents being owned, and it has ways of making that known.
Old wives say something like this chooses its victims, not the other way around.
You can feel it watching you from inside your pack, waiting for the right moment.
It grants strength, yes - but strength borrowed always comes due.
The {noun} belonged to a man who insisted it was harmless. He was wrong.
The previous owner of this {noun} had excellent taste and terrible luck.
The {noun} has outlived at least three people who claimed they understood it.
Someone once tried to destroy the {noun}. Judging by the repairs, it did not go well for them.
The {noun} was stolen from a tomb. The thief was later found several miles away, still holding it.
The previous owner left a note beside the {noun}: 'Not again.'
The {noun} was sold cheaply by its previous owner. He refused to explain why.
The previous owner of this {noun} disappeared shortly after claiming it had started whispering.
The {noun} has been owned by priests, thieves, nobles, and at least one fool. You may now add your name to the list.
An old merchant refused to sell the {noun}, then gave it away for free. He looked relieved.
The {noun} was found in a dungeon beside a pile of identical keys. None of them fit anything.
According to its previous owner, the {noun} was perfectly safe. According to everyone else, he was an idiot.
The {noun} was recovered from the belongings of an adventurer who had apparently packed for everything except survival.
Someone clearly cared for the {noun}. The deep bite marks around its edge suggest it was not entirely mutual.
Legends claim the {noun} belonged to a king who had no kingdom left by the time he died.
knowledge: Whatever knowledge it holds was never meant to be understood by the living.
Reading it feels like remembering something that never happened to you.
Every page, every rune, seems to cost something to understand.
The wisdom inside is real. So is the price for keeping it.
haunting: {name} did not rest easy, and neither, it seems, does what he left behind.
There is a presence bound to it - patient, cold, and not entirely gone.
Sometimes, in the dark, you swear you hear it breathing.
It was not meant to be carried alone. It no longer is.
lore: {name} killed his brother with this {noun}. His brother's ghost supposedly follows whoever carries it.
It is said the owner never let this {noun} out of his sight, not even in death.
The last owner's name was scratched out of every record that mentions this {noun}.
Legend credits {name} with both its making and its ruin, though no two tellings agree which came first.
{name}'s name is carved into it in letters too small to have been written by human hands.
guardian: It was carried by those sworn to protect something greater than themselves.
Whatever it once guarded is long gone. The habit of guarding, however, remains.
It seems to settle, almost gratefully, into the hands of someone willing to stand and hold a line.
blessing: Rare among things pulled from the dark, this one seems to mean you well.
It carries no weight of malice - only the quiet favor of something long forgotten.
Holding it feels, for once, like being looked after rather than watched.
loss_note: Something about it draws on your own vitality just to remain whole.
You feel a little thinner, a little less yourself, the longer you carry it.
It borrows from your strength to keep its secrets intact.
